features.name: any_comment_explicit_example_label
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain an explicitly labeled example phrase such as "example:" or "one example is"?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings (missing/malformed -> null; empty list -> 0). Return 1 if any comment matches, case-insensitive, regex r'\b(for example|for instance|e\.g\.|one example|an example|example\s*:|examples\s*:|example\s+\d+\s*:|here is an example|here\'s an example)' ... restricted to explicit labels: r'(\bexamples?\s*:|\b(one|another|a|an|first|second)\s+example\s+(is|would be|being)\b|\bhere(\'s| is)\s+an\s+example\b)'. Otherwise 0. Raw text matching; no semantic filtering.

h0: any_comment_explicit_example_label is unrelated to the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Discussions with at least one counter-argument containing an explicitly labeled example have higher probability of OP view change.
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as delta (OP view change) at discussion row level; no per-comment outcomes are supplied, so the association is row-level only. Label detection is literal regex (a narrow set of explicit labels such as 'example:' and 'one example is'); unlabeled examples and generic 'for example' are not counted. Raw text may include quoted text or outcome announcements; not outcome-free, and reply timing is unknown. Association only, not causal.
